commits.body:
Implement the user's requested direct-to-main recovery work, preserving the
existing unpublished planning history and the Epic 43 authoring service.

Requirements and design decisions:
- Epic 40: a material owned Task body revision records old/new content hashes
  and its commit, permits one dispatch generation, and retains prior execution
  attempts. Repeated revisions do not buy another retry. Explicit contracts
  confined to Task-denied deliverables report a structured scope blocker before
  dispatch. Live leases, normal dispatch gates and path guards remain binding.
- Epic 41: recovery identity includes current heads, validation, queue, owner,
  status and checkpoint observations. Recheck these facts before cache reuse.
  Reserve the recovery-created queued state as the same generation; replay a
  stale handoff after restart without replacing the Task or its workspace.
  Resolve Feature identity from the Task document and reject revision tokens.
- Epic 42: route semantic conflicts to the concrete source Task with its Feature
  supervisor. Restore the owned worktree in a fresh process, acknowledge the
  request, integrate the current Feature, validate exact tested ancestry, rearm
  the original action, and retain failed attempts through canonical completion.
  Preserve unrelated sibling blockers. Derived monitoring blockage is not an
  execution veto on the child integration that can resolve it; manual blockage
  and ordinary approval/dependency gates still apply. not_active is retryable.
- Replace the single-deliverable-commit refusal with additive recovery commits
  when history includes integration/lifecycle commits. Protected parent files
  staged by a merge are accepted only when unchanged from the parent tree.
  No reset, clean, cross-team write permission, or Task force-push is introduced.
- Validation uses repository [validation].command argv, with generic pytest as
  the default and existing scoped pytest commands supported. Remove Cascade's
  own review-test filename from the publication contract. Test evidence cannot
  claim a Feature head absent from the tested Task tree.
- Persist concrete owned incidents for review fetch, worktree, mergeability and
  admission failures. Expose local Task delivery reviews, validation/action
  evidence, and direct-family messaging and supervision tools. Waiting and
  blocked deliveries do not consume execution slots.
- Share a reentrant cross-process lifecycle lock across execution, action and
  recovery writers so independent MCP and supervisor processes preserve state.
- Epic 43: expose canonical revisioned manifest authoring only through trusted
  Epic planning roles, scoped to the live owned worktree. Reject scope overrides,
  stale revisions and incomplete environments. Missing-manifest UI/prompt
  guidance names the authoring operation; none_required remains explicit.
  Declaration never grants installation or upgrade approval.

Validation: focused acceptance, real Git conflict/restart/merge regressions,
revision concurrency, cross-process ledger writers, UI projection/syntax, and
normal dispatch tests. Recovery acceptance stubs only the model provider and
crosses actual graph/kickoff, scoped tools, validation, queue and merge paths.
The broad suite also exposes pre-existing missing-manifest and provider fixture
failures; representative failures reproduce in an unchanged baseline worktree.

Pass InstallationBinding.from_entry to the existing approval boundary, preserving exact approval and policy checks. This repairs seven failing operation-authority tests; all eleven now pass.

Extend Epic 41 acceptance through two busy merge refusals and ordinary periodic stale-queue invalidation before the real resume, validation, and exactly-once merge path. The combined closure regression run passes 35 tests. This evidence supports closing Epic 41; it does not assert that Epics 40, 42, or 43 satisfy every remaining criterion.

commits.body:
Record acceptance evidence for stale-delivery recovery, including repeated busy refusals, periodic invalidation, real checkpoint resume, current-base validation, and exactly-once merge. The operator authorized direct delivery on main; close the verified brief without fabricating child Feature plans or a review that did not occur.

Keep Epics 40, 42, and 43 open with explicit remaining requirements. Do not waive material-revision semantics, safe-worktree checks, executable review recovery, terminal delivery visibility, or full dependency lifecycle acceptance. Correct the earlier overbroad implementation claim and preserve the active Epic 43 plan.

commits.body:
Canonicalize dependency-state locking to the tracking trunk so planning authors in an owned Epic worktree serialize with human approval and trusted execution. Retain explicit per-dependency human authorization; declarations do not grant installation or execution authority.

Prove both planning roles, real dependency approval and bounded trusted execution through sign-off/plan approval/feature dispatch, expected-revision races, fresh-process restart, split product/tracking repositories, and owning-worktree isolation. Browser coverage suppresses manifest-dependent controls while declaration is missing. These complete the audited Epic 43 gaps alongside the InstallationBinding correction in bc615b88; no acceptance requirement is waived.
commits.subject: fix: complete Epic 43 manifest authority and lifecycle acceptance

commits.body:
Task revisions must change the executable contract: deterministic scope failures require changed authorized deliverables, cosmetic edits do not grant a retry, and external permission refusals remain independent. Persist revision intent before its document commit for crash replay. Dispatch rechecks leases, dependencies, parent pins and branch/worktree scope under the lifecycle lock. Cleanliness means inspecting preserved work, not rejecting every dirty checkout: the existing Task may finish its guarded source changes without reset, clean, replacement, or expanded path authority.

Make owned review-health incidents executable through current-head admission and the existing publication tool. Return the health action that can actually retry when admission refuses, along with the concrete admission blocker. Reconcile healed incidents, create a new generation on recurrence, persist acknowledgement, retain failed validation/publication history, and expose terminal Task validation and action evidence. Preload delivery state once per board render.

Canonicalize lifecycle locks and execution/action/orphan/merge-queue storage across trunk and owned worktrees. Carry trusted product/tracking repository context through both MCP subprocess transports; keep source edits and diff operations in the product repository. No approval, exact-head, team ownership, or Task path gate is weakened.

Acceptance includes denied planning scope -> revised source contract -> one real supervised delivery; crash after revision commit; additive semantic conflict repair detecting the wrong process_lock, then eleven passing checks; restart after acknowledgement; unrelated sibling blocker preservation; review admission/fetch/worktree/validation recovery; completed team wakeup and historical dispatch authority; and actual split-repository MCP workers. Broader affected suite: 164 passed. Final boundary suite: 33 passed; final review suite: 8 passed; store/action/MCP suites also passed. Repair the legacy failure-test provider fixture so it reaches its intended ownership assertion.
commits.subject: fix: complete supervised Task and review recovery for Epics 40 and 42

commits.body:
Record final acceptance and design choices for completed Epics 40 and 42 and preserve the full active Epic 43 architecture, approved plan, and existing child work breakdown on main. Reconcile its Features and Tasks to the operator-authorized direct delivery, without fabricating forge reviews or claiming their runtime branches were merged.

The earlier partial-completion audit remains historical evidence and is explicitly superseded by final delivery through a37f05ff and b421d160. Epic 41 was already closed with its acceptance evidence. No requirement is waived. Retain old Epic 43 runtime worktrees, branches, and uncommitted evidence while retiring their active registry entries so stale planning copies cannot resume duplicate work after restart.

Explain unavailable support and prevent newly enabling unsupported Flex.

Keep new-brief capability gating and the normal edit-review workflow. Add regression coverage for loading an unsupported enabled setting, disabling it without changing model selections, rerendering, edit payload creation, and persisted frontmatter. Four focused UI/live-server/editor tests passed; the extended persistence test passed. Verified updated HTML and JavaScript are served by the running healthy War Room without restarting teams.

commits.body:
Bring Feature 013001 implementation onto main while preserving trunk lifecycle documents and unrelated completed specifications. Its original public Feature history remains an ancestor; teams can continue the approved stacked sequence.

Requirement clarification: auditors must inventory canonical registered tracking worktrees, including unstarted child Tasks, and must use the owning recovery capability's failure class. Human/manual blockers retain refusal semantics. Preserve bounded fair paging and cached completed inventories.

Separate auditor receipts from authoritative incident generations to prevent diagnostic feedback loops. Capability arrival retires older missing receipts for the same owner and operation. Reserve against a scoped local fingerprint of plans, comments, execution, actions, reviews and registrations; exclude derived heartbeat age and perform no Git or network work under the lifecycle lock. Recheck changes to children and gates, not merely the owner's status.

Validation: 80 audit, capability, reservation, health and real Task recovery tests passed, including real observation/probe/reservation and changed-child admission races. Live read-only inventory finds all Epic 13 Features and Feature 002 Tasks with no missing-document errors.
commits.subject: fix: integrate Epic 13 audit foundations with usable recovery admission

commits.body:
A Feature can finish one planning turn and start another in about127 ms, starving the watchdog's child merge retries. Service only that Feature's validated delivery queue at the completed-turn boundary while retaining its graph lock and normal source, target, cleanliness and evidence guards. Busy parent/source turns defer scheduling before consuming durable recovery attempts.

A team may also finish an integration repair during its own turn. Acknowledge an already-integrated base without mutation after verifying the owned checkout, clean merge state and exact ancestry; retain busy refusal when an actual merge is needed.

Validation: 2 real delivery/recovery regressions, 5 serialized queue race tests, 13 Task recovery generation regressions, and the existing clean Epic update test passed. Queue fixtures now select offered provider models and create undispatched children in backlog, matching current activation requirements.
commits.subject: fix: give validated deliveries priority between parent planning turns

commits.body:
Epic planners could read child Features on trunk but received content_access_denied after dispatch moved the canonical spec to a sibling worktree. Feature planners had the equivalent direct-Task problem, and local inherited copies could return stale briefs.

Resolve scoped reads through the canonical document checkout and admit only the fresh authoritative direct-child path. This restores the existing intended parent-read contract; it does not grant writes, unrelated-team reads, Epic grandchild bodies, symlink aliases or noncanonical sibling copies.

Validation: 46 focused guard, scoped-document and dependency-boundary tests passed, followed by 2 real registered-worktree regressions covering all four parent planning roles and preserved denials. One broader legacy mint fixture remains blocked by its missing dependency manifest, after its read/write assertions pass.
commits.subject: fix: let parent teams read current direct-child worktree plans

commits.body: PR206 is merged and all six Tasks are completed. Preserve their terminal plans and handoff artifact on trunk so worktree retirement and parent-base synchronization cannot hide the accepted Feature from the board. The earlier code-only integration intentionally preserved trunk documents; this follows through with the now-accepted lifecycle records and keeps unrelated completed work intact. No work status is inferred from pending review.
commits.subject: docs: retain merged Feature 013001 delivery records on main

commits.body:
Respect canonical blocking comments, explicit human gates and authoritative dependency outcomes before classifying unresolved actions. Cancelled dependencies remain unsatisfied. Apply the same gates to derived child incidents while allowing an independent failed sibling to proceed.

Read current registered document and comment locations without mutating the registry. Fingerprint ancestor comments and child dependencies so a gate arriving between observation and admission invalidates the reservation using local reads only under the lifecycle lock. Pending review alone remains a wait, but does not suppress a concrete repair.

Validation: 53 audit, capability, reservation and protected-wait tests passed locally, including all 14 new regression cases; investigator broader focused run passed 85 tests. Existing comments and optional API fixture failures were reproduced on unchanged HEAD.
commits.subject: fix: distinguish protected waits from actionable audit incidents

commits.body:
Task 013002003 repeatedly passed supervised tests on dirty changes, committed afterward, and exhausted retries because the tool returned only exit code zero while the finalizer reported tests_not_run. Keep exact-head validation intact: report delivery_ready=false and an explicit commit-then-test next step when a green run lacks final evidence. Explain ordering and complete pytest argv in the actual MCP catalog and SWE/retry prompts.

Read the durable final_validation_required or tests_red result when finalizing an out-of-process tool turn, instead of relying on process-local test memory. Regression checks exercise real dirty tests, committed exact-head tests, and an MCP-style missing-evidence retry. Validation: 25 relevant task tool/graph/prompt tests passed; broader run exposed pre-existing provider inventory and stale lambda fixture errors.
commits.subject: fix: explain and preserve final committed validation requirements

commits.body:
A health retry retained retry_task's outer lifecycle flock across dispatch's
boot and synchronous SWE kickoff. The provider's MCP tools then waited for the
same flock while the supervisor waited for the provider, preventing both Task
progress and board reads. The sweep also retained its broad process lock.

Keep admission atomic inside dispatch_task, which already rechecks retry
eligibility, ownership leases, dependencies, comments, scope and capacity. Add
an expected-parent check there so moving the ownership check outside the lock
cannot authorize a Task whose parent changed. Queue recovery model turns using
the existing supervised deferred-kickoff path after dispatch releases its lock.

Collect health remediation candidates under the sweep lock, then claim and
recheck each incident in a short ledger transaction. Execute retry outside the
sweep lock and serialize final ledger updates separately. Concurrent sweeps may
report the same observed snapshot; the durable incident claim still permits
only one dispatch. This preserves history and gates rather than bypassing busy
owners or clearing state.

Validation: 42 existing recovery/health/dispatch tests passed; the remaining
concurrent observation-count assertion was updated for the new lock boundary.
Six final concurrency and lock-scope regressions passed, including independent
MCP subprocess reads during a still-running provider turn, unlocked boot hooks,
nonblocking recovery handoff, one dispatch under concurrent requests, durable
failure dedupe, and direct-parent changes at admission. git diff --check passed.
commits.subject: fix: release recovery locks before starting Task turns

commits.body:
Publishing validated queue evidence cleared the Task's derived parent blocker,
which committed the Feature document and moved the exact target head that the
just-completed supervised tests had certified. The finished-turn replay then
rejected its own handoff as stale and requested another validation turn.

Keep queue publication free of parent-document mutations. Reconcile matching
Task delivery blockers after a successful or already-proven canonical merge,
before the existing completion rollup. The merge target preflight already
allows recovery into a parent blocked by derived monitoring; no new bypass or
validation exception is required. Manual blockage, human comments, unrelated
sibling incidents and exact source/target validation remain authoritative. Red
tests never clear blockers, and changed Feature code still requires fresh tests.

Validation: five new real-worktree regressions cover unchanged validated heads,
finished-turn replay, exactly one normal merge, preserved sibling/manual/comment
gates, and red-test preservation. Six existing generation/restart/conflict
recovery cases and four exact-head/stale/red validation boundary tests passed.
Two final positive cases also assert no TaskValidationRetryRequested event.
git diff --check passed. No live Task, Feature or runtime state was changed.
commits.subject: fix: reconcile Task delivery blockers only after merge

commits.body:
A live Epic 13 Task passed supervised validation, continued editing review fixes,
and was merged from its older committed snapshot. Delivery freshness compared
only branch SHAs, while the busy guard expected swe messages instead of the real
task_swe checkpoint node. Normal successful teardown could then force-remove the
checkout and discard those later edits. The isolated real tool/finalizer fixture
reproduced that data loss.

Require the registered source checkout to remain clean and outside an unfinished
Git operation when replaying validation or admitting a merge. Task write tools
withdraw old readiness immediately; native/index/untracked edits are also checked
at finalization, queue admission, and the locked merge boundary. Later work returns
to the original Task through its durable input queue and same execution attempt;
ordinary deferral spends neither the merge-attempt nor validation-failure budget.
An edit arriving after preflight remains retryable rather than a terminal blocker.
Recognize actual pending task_swe nodes, including a first turn without an earlier
role message; delivery resumes after the graph checkpoint finishes.

Cleanup independently preserves dirty worktrees and registrations and uses normal
Git removal without --force, so a write racing cleanup cannot authorize data loss.
Read source registrations from the canonical product trunk without creating new
registry files in owned checkouts. Existing human/comment gates, validated commit
identities, Task branches, and approval decisions remain authoritative. No new
human approval or replacement Task is required to finish preserved work.

Validation: 49 distinct targeted tests passed, including 13 new real regressions
for tool/native/staged/untracked edits, exactly one same-Task completion after
fresh validation, direct merge and teardown preservation, actual LangGraph busy
and idle checkpoints, a write arriving at the merge boundary, and owned-checkout
lookup without a process cache. Existing blocker, worktree, guard, delivery fairness,
and six generation/restart/conflict recovery variants passed. Ruff and diff checks
passed. Isolated fixtures now commit their ignore configuration so pytest cache
files do not masquerade as user changes. No live work was discarded or rewritten.
commits.subject: fix: preserve post-validation Task edits through delivery and teardown

commits.body:
Epic13's Task005 had current green delivery evidence and an idle Task checkpoint,
but its Feature owner spent more than20minutes inspecting that child and sleeping.
The parent's active planning turn prevented the queued merge it was waiting for.
supervise_child returned a generic instruction to wait for execution progress and
did not expose the between-turn delivery boundary.

Expose parent_turn_boundary for nonterminal, queued awaiting-merge deliveries and
explicitly ask the planning owner to finish its turn rather than poll or sleep.
Planning directives now distinguish completing actionable owned work from waiting
inside a turn for children, delivery or external review; ordinary supervisor events
wake the team for subsequent work. Retain all busy, clean-checkout, exact-validation,
permission and comment gates. This corrects the coordination contract rather than
merging into a concurrently owned checkout or adding another recovery engine.

Validation:17 targeted Feature recovery and delivery-fairness checks passed. A new
real-worktree/LangGraph regression proves active-parent inspection reports the yield
step without spending a merge attempt or changing Task state, then the same queued
delivery merges exactly once after the parent checkpoint finishes. Existing retry,
permission, ownership and fairness contracts passed; Ruff and diff checks passed.
The observed polling owner eventually yielded normally; no provider was terminated.
commits.subject: fix: explain when planning owners must yield for child delivery

commits.body: Feature 002 completed all tasks but publication rejected a legacy task without a trailer whose task-side parent was itself a merge. Preserve the existing legacy fast path, then resolve the full durable validated range when it cannot select one single-parent commit. Require the same task identity, branch and Feature ancestry, validated base, and implementation changes. This changes publication recovery only, not feature requirements or approval gates. Validation: all 12 publication tests pass, including a real merge-shaped legacy history regression.

commits.body: When patch replay conflicts, a validated Task may have entered the Feature by fast-forward and therefore have no dedicated integration merge. Reuse its ancestor source snapshot only when it excludes every later Task; the final publication tree remains the original Feature tree. This unblocks Feature 002 review publication without changing feature code or gates. Validation: 12 publication tests pass; canonical publication successfully opened PR 207.

work_items.narrative:
# Functional MVP

Ship a local CascadeCode that can run one real Epic → Feature → Task loop against this repo. The operator talks in a War Room, plans live as markdown on a filesystem board, and nothing is implemented unless the human or the Boss dispatches it.

This epic is **active** (human, 2026-10-09). feat_001 through feat_015 are completed ([feat_015](../../features/3_completed/feat_015_provider_backends.md) — provider backends and credentials). The epic file stays in `2_active` until the human confirms epic completion (`confirm_epic_complete`).

## Intent

An operator on this machine can:

1. Open a local UI bound to localhost.
2. Activate this epic (or another) themselves.
3. Sit with an Epic Team that mints Feature specs into backlog and stops.
4. Dispatch a Feature (human or Boss). Drop in, comment, read the decision log.
5. Watch a Feature Team lock APIs and mint Tasks into backlog — never into `2_active`.
6. Adjudicate a `propose_epic_amendment` in a split-diff pane.
7. Dispatch a Task. A SWE agent commits on `task/{id}`. The operator merges locally.
8. See cards move. Features and the Epic cannot close with open comment threads.

While this epic is still open, the same operator can also:

9. Run each roster role through a local provider backend (Cursor SDK, or the Claude / Codex CLI if that binary is already on this machine), with an explicit provider and model id on every call. Cascade does not install those CLIs. Remote agent VMs are out.
10. Set project default models *per provider* for epic agents, feature agents, and task agents, and override provider or model on a single epic, feature, or task. Sign in from the War Room so the operator does not edit `.netrc` or a file in the workspace.
11. Collapse completed feature and task cards, and focus the board on one epic's features and one feature's tasks.
12. Open any epic, feature, or task plan from the board via **View plan** — rendered markdown in the War Room, including Mermaid diagrams when the viewer bundles Mermaid locally.
13. Run every roster role with default in-repo philosophy playbooks (frugal engineering; PM/EM/developer/reviewer briefs mapped onto Cascade roles), so agents optimize for reliability and delivery speed rather than vanity coverage or pedantic review.
14. Point Cascade at this repo or another local git repo. Agents start only on authorized kickoff edges. An active epic lives on `epic/{id}`, an in-progress feature lives on `feat/{id}`, and tasks are parallel branches into that feature. The War Room reads the worktree dispatch already created. Clicking a card does not check out a branch in the operator's directory. The supervisor shows which features are in flight and which paths overlap.

Success is that loop, on this repo or on another local git repo the operator points Cascade at. Success is **not** a hosted product, a GitLab integration, auto-merge, or one supervisor driving several repos.

## Macro-architecture

Four process kinds, one local repo:

```
localhost UI ──► workspace principals (Human, Boss)
                      │
                      ▼
                 watchdog + queue     (deterministic)
                      │
          ┌───────────┼───────────┐
          ▼           ▼           ▼
     Epic graph  Feature graph  Task graph
          │           │           │
          └───────────┴───────────┘
                      │
                      ▼
              /docs board + git
```

- **Board** (`/docs/{epics,features,tasks}/{1_backlog,2_active,3_completed}`) is lifecycle. Folder membership is status. No parallel status database.
- **Plans** are markdown + YAML frontmatter. Edits are local git commits. Children pin `parent_rev` to a SHA.
- **Queue** (`/docs/_queue/{graph_id}.jsonl`) is the only cross-graph channel. Typed events only. No shared transcripts.
- **Comments** live in `/docs/_comments/{doc_id}.jsonl`, not in the plan body.
- **Watchdog** is not an LLM. It watches the board, enforces dispatch law, boots and tears down graphs.
- **Graphs** are LangGraph subgraphs, one per work object, separate checkpointers.
- **Models.** Each roster role calls a local provider backend with an explicit provider and model id. Project defaults live in `cascade.toml` per provider. An epic, feature, or task may override them. Boot resolves both ids. The agent does not pick another provider or model.
- **UI** is local only. Default home is the Epic War Room. Feature rooms exist after attach. Task graphs have no room. The board can collapse completed columns and lens features and tasks by the epic or feature in focus. Each board card exposes **View plan** to read the on-disk markdown body (Mermaid supported in the renderer). For an in-progress epic or feature, that disk is the team's integration worktree. Attach and View plan do not check out a branch in the operator's directory.

Planning teams write artifacts. They do not start the next machine.

## Cross-module constraints

1. **Local only.** UI binds `127.0.0.1`. No cloud checkpointer, no remote agent runtime, no GitHub/GitLab client. Task output is a local branch. A provider token authenticates a local backend; it does not start a hosted agent that outlives the turn.
2. **Filesystem is truth.** Agents and UI both watch directories. Inventing a second board is a defect.
3. **Dispatch law.** Epic → `ready_to_plan` / `2_active`: human only. Feature planning start and Task dispatch: human or Boss. Epic Team and Feature Team have no dispatch tool and cannot `mv` a child into `2_active`.
4. **Dependencies.** `depends_on` on the `.md` (frontmatter **and** body). Dispatch is illegal until every listed ID is in `3_completed`. Cycles fail validation.
5. **Parallelism.** `cascade.toml` `task_parallelism` (default 4). Watchdog counts Tasks in `2_active` whose status is `active` (not `blocked`). Over-cap dispatches wait; they do not start.
6. **Git versions plans.** No integer `rev`. `parent_rev` is a commit SHA. Amendment accept commits the Epic and sends that SHA down.
7. **Context isolation.** A graph loads only its doc, allowed parents, its comments, and its queue. Path sandbox enforces tool scopes. Prompting is not enough.
8. **Decisions outlive chat.** Locking a constraint, API, type, flow, or amendment requires `record_decision` on the owning `.md`.
9. **Comments default to non-blocking.** Any open human thread still blocks Feature/Epic completion. A human (only) may mark a comment `blocking`, which pauses `mint_task` on that Feature. It does not freeze dispatch of already-minted Tasks. Agents cannot set `blocking`.
10. **Task skills, not a stack enum.** A Task may list in-repo `SKILL.md` paths. Empty list = general SWE agent. Feature Team may set them at mint; Human/Boss may override at dispatch. Missing or out-of-repo paths fail dispatch. No classifier, no `cuda|cpp|python` label.
11. **Failure policy.** Infra/tool flakes inside a live Task subgraph retry at most twice, then `TaskFailed`. Test or spec misses fail closed immediately (no intra-run retry). `TaskFailed` toasts Feature room + War Room, sets status `blocked` (file stays in `2_active`), and tears the graph down. `blocked` does not count toward the parallelism cap. Re-dispatch is a new Human or Boss `dispatch_task` — Feature/Epic cannot restart. The Boss may propose a retry; it must not auto-fire `dispatch_task` on a failed id.
12. **Explicit local backend.** Roster roles infer through a local provider backend (`cursor`, `claude`, or `codex`). Every call carries a provider id and a model id. Cloud agent VMs, remote checkpointers, and remote brokers stay forbidden. Cascade does not install provider CLIs; a missing binary fails the turn.
13. **Model defaults are per provider.** `cascade.toml` names a default provider and, for each provider, default models for epic agents, feature agents, and task agents. The work document may override provider and/or model. A feature does not inherit its epic's override. Unset config fails closed. It does not silently become `auto`.
14. **Board lens.** The War Room can collapse completed columns. Features shown belong to the selected epic, or to epics in `2_active` when none is selected. Tasks shown belong to the feature selected on the board. The read API still returns the full board.
15. **One workspace, one repo.** A Cascade process supervises a single git root. The tool and that root may be different directories. Agents start only on an authorized kickoff edge. Minting a file and polling the board do not start an agent. One process does not orchestrate multiple repos.
16. **Stacked integration lines.** The product trunk holds the human brief and, later, a promoted epic. `activate_epic` cuts `epic/{id}` from that brief. `dispatch_feature` cuts `feat/{id}` from the epic branch. `dispatch_task` cuts `task/{id}` from the feature branch. Each live epic and feature has a worktree under `.cascade/worktrees/`. The operator checkout stays on the trunk. Task branches merge into the feature, the feature merges into the epic branch once, and the epic branch merges to the trunk when the human promotes it. The supervisor reports in-flight features, the paths they change, and path overlaps. Overlap does not dispatch or merge.
17. **Provider credentials stay off the board.** Tokens live in the `up` process environment (still first) or a user-level store the War Room login pane writes (`~/.cascade/credentials`, mode `0600`). An already-logged-in Claude or Codex CLI session is a third source. Never `.netrc`, never `cascade.toml`, never a file in the workspace. One missing credential fails that provider's turn; Cascade does not silently switch providers.

| Python 3.12+ | Supervisor, watchdog, LangGraph runtimes |
| LangGraph | One subgraph per work object; checkpointer per id |
| Local git | Plan versioning; integration branches `epic/{id}`, `feat/{id}`, `task/{id}` |
| `cascade.toml` | Supervisor config; planning agents do not use it to self-start |

| `~/.cascade/credentials` | User-level store written by War Room login; mode `0600`; not per-project |

Forbidden: remote brokers, cloud agent VMs, cloud checkpointers, installing provider CLIs from Cascade, writing tokens to `.netrc` or the repo, and writing task code onto the trunk or the epic branch instead of `task/{id}`. work_items.narrative:
# Plan-view review threads

## Intent

Give the operator **GitHub-style review on the plan page**: select text or a section in **View plan**, start a thread, and have the **owning agent team** (Epic or Feature) respond — update the plan, answer the question, push back, or record a decision. Threads stay on the plan surface instead of only in War Room chat.

**Human gate:** a thread that touches open product decisions must be **resolved by a human** before work that would rely on those decisions proceeds. That includes minting tasks, dispatching features/tasks, and merges when the thread’s scope covers the affected doc sections or downstream children.

This epic extends the existing comment sidecar (`docs/_comments/{doc_id}.jsonl`, feat_005) and plan viewer (feat_012). It does **not** replace Epic chat or amendments; it is the async, plan-anchored path for “talk to the team about this paragraph.”

Operator success:

1. Open `/plan/epic_002` (or any epic/feature plan) and leave an inline or section-anchored comment without attaching to a live room.
2. See the Epic Team or Feature Team reply in-thread; optionally see the markdown body or decision log update after the agent turn.
3. Mark a thread **resolved** only as human; unresolved **blocking** threads visibly stop dispatch/merge for scoped work.
4. Use the same UX for epic plans (Epic Team owns) and feature plans (Feature Team owns).

## Macro-architecture

```
Plan viewer (GET /plan/{id})
  ├─ renders markdown body (existing)
  ├─ loads GET /api/comments/{doc_id}  [feat_016 shipped]
  ├─ inline / section anchors + thread UI  [feat_017 shipped]
  └─ POST /api/comment (root or parent reply); POST /api/comment/resolve  [feat_018 shipped]

docs/_comments/{doc_id}.jsonl          [unchanged store; richer anchor fields]
        │
        ▼ CommentPosted / CommentReplied
Epic graph or Feature graph (owning doc_id)
        │
        ├─ reply_comment / write_doc / record_decision
        ├─ resolve is human-only, thread-level (feat_018 shipped); agents do not get the tool
        └─ optional: propose_epic_amendment when epic section changes

Watchdog deliver_queue_kickoffs → kickoff_turn(kind="comment") for human authors (feat_020 shipped, task_088–089)
  HTTP POST enqueues only; skipped events still ingest the queue offset (dec_021–dec_025)
  Graph boots like War Room attach into resolve_doc_worktree — never trunk (dec_023)
  In-thread reply_comment on the triggering comment is required; spec edit is not a substitute (dec_024)
  Watchdog/kickoff never write the sidecar; reply is the existing agent tool (dec_025)

Dispatch law + new scope gates (feat_019 shipped, task_083–085)
  ├─ cascade.comments.blocking_threads_for live-loads work+ancestors; refuse dispatch/mint_task/merge
  └─ completion rollup unchanged: any open human thread still blocks closeout
  Agent resolve_comment is unregistered (feat_018 shipped; dec_013 leak closed)
```

**Owning team:** epic-tier `doc_id` → graph `epic_{id}`; feature-tier `doc_id` → graph `feat_{id}`. Task plans are read-only for comments in v1 (tasks have no room; operator comments on parent feature or epic).

## Cross-module constraints

- **Filesystem is truth.** Comments remain sidecars, not inline in the `.md` body (feat_005 / DESIGN §10.3).
- **Localhost only.** Plan viewer and APIs stay on `127.0.0.1`; no GitHub OAuth or remote PR comments.
- **Dispatch law unchanged:** Epic activate = human only; feature/task dispatch = human or Boss. Agents still cannot dispatch themselves.
- **Kickoff edges only:** Posting a comment enqueues `CommentPosted`; one agent turn is delivered by the watchdog — no timer polling for “new comments on main.” HTTP POST does not start a turn (dec_011, dec_012, dec_021–dec_025, dec_027). Resolve POST also does not start a turn (dec_011, dec_020). Do not add HTTP `kickoff_graph_queue_event` to “fix” cold start. **feat_016 D4/D5 “keep HTTP kickoff at merge” is void (dec_027)** — do not treat that completed spec as the live contract. Filter lives inside existing `deliver_queue_kickoffs`; skipped events still advance the offset (dec_023). `kickoff_turn` returns like live chat — do not wait for `reply_comment` (dec_025).
- **Stacked worktrees:** Comment sidecars for an active epic/feature live in the same git root as that team’s plan (`resolve_doc_worktree` / existing comment repo rules). A comment `kickoff_turn` uses that same worktree as the graph workspace (dec_005, dec_023); trunk pointers never get a sidecar.
- **Read-only plan renderer** may gain comment *chrome*; plan body edits still go through agent tools or git, not WYSIWYG in the viewer (feat_012 read-only stance unless explicitly extended).
- **Comment chrome is render-only (dec_016).** `line_start` / `line_end` are 1-based markdown source lines from the renderer token source map. Re-anchor and outdated never rewrite the sidecar. `#plan-comments` is upserted by `data-comment-id`, never replaced via `innerHTML`. Task-tier GET `/api/comments` 400 stays. **feat_017 shipped this** (task_080–082). **feat_018 shipped the Resolve button** on that list; do not add a second panel.
- **Blocking is human-only** on create (existing store rule). Agents may reply but not resolve or set blocking. feat_018 shipped the store+tool guard and the Resolve button; `resolve_comment` is unregistered. The dec_013 leak is closed. feat_020 must not re-register the tool (task_088–089 did not).
- **Comment turns are watchdog-only (dec_011, dec_012, dec_021–dec_025, dec_027). feat_020 shipped this** (task_088–089). Filter lives inside existing `deliver_queue_kickoffs` (not a second subscriber). It starts `kickoff_turn(kind="comment")` only for human `CommentPosted` / `CommentReplied`. Agent replies and `CommentResolved` ingest the queue offset and do not start a turn; skipped events must still advance the cursor. Offset is exactly-once — no `kicked_off` sidecar flag. One turn per matching event, owning graph only (`epic_{id}` / `feat_{id}` from `doc_id`); do not fan-out to parent epic, child features, or iterate owners/roles. Empty or never-attached graphs still boot **the same way War Room attach does**: same roster/skills/tools (`resolve_comment` stays unregistered; existing `reply_comment` stays registered), workspace `resolve_doc_worktree(doc_id)` — never trunk, never a throwaway worktree, never a headless comment runner. `kind="comment"` is a KickoffReason tag only; the turn path is the existing planning turn (same speaker selection as live chat). Author filter is the event/sidecar `author` field (`human` only). `KickoffReason.message` is `{role: "human", content: ...}` with the **shipped** feat_020-spec shape `cmt_NNN on {doc_id} #{section} [blocking]\n{body}` (dec_027; dec_024/025 four-line prefix is planning history). Playbook is one short section on the existing `product_manager` skill (loaded by that boot, not injected as a system prompt, not copied onto architect skills). Always `reply_comment` in-thread with the existing tool `comment_id` = the triggering comment id (dec_024, dec_025); a spec/decision edit is not a substitute. `write_doc` remains optional. No comment-failure toast/spinner. No HTTP eager turn, no generic `queue_event` kickoff, no comment-only role, no digest/batch, no second writer, no poll/spinner for the agent reply. If `kickoff_turn` raises, keep the event (existing watchdog retry).
- **Comment reply write-path (dec_025, shipped).** `deliver_queue_kickoffs` and `kickoff_turn` never call `reply_comment` and never append the sidecar (no auto-ack). The in-thread reply is only the existing feat_004/005 `reply_comment(comment_id, body)` tool during the existing planning turn — `comment_id` is the parent (the triggering event’s comment id, not the thread root and not the human row’s parent). Do not add a `parent` kwarg, a `review_comment` facade, or a second reply tool. Agents never POST `/api/comment` (that route is always `author=human` and would loop). Stored author is the speaking role already in the feat_016 enum (`epic_manager` / `feature_lead` / …), never `human`, never a new `comment-reviewer`. `kickoff_turn` returns like live chat; offset advances when kickoff is accepted, not when a sidecar reply appears. Do not skip a turn because the thread was resolved before the agent spoke; do not un-resolve. Restore the existing `reply_comment` registration if missing; do not add a `kind="comment"` allowlist.
- **Gate is store-only and shipped (dec_017, dec_018, dec_019).** `cascade.comments.blocking_threads_for(work_id)` is a pure function next to the comment store. Each call live-loads open blocking roots from the work and ancestors via sidecar + `resolve_doc_worktree` (never trunk pointers, never a boot-time cache, never plan-viewer JS). It reads current worktree `##+` headings. It does not consult outdated state, line numbers, or rewrite comments. Replaced the existing `mint_task` any-blocking check; do not stack it back. Do not gate `mint_feature` or `activate_epic`. Closeout rollup stays separate. Merge means the existing feature/task integration merge for that `work_id`, not git commit. Do not re-implement the gate.
- **Scope (locked, see dec_003/dec_004/dec_008/dec_010/dec_018):** affected work for an open blocking *root* thread, in order of precedence:
  (a) explicit `blocks: [work_id, …]` on the root comment, if **non-empty**: exclusive membership of those ids plus tasks of any listed feature (unknown ids ignored). Do not also apply (b) or (c);
  (b) else, *section thread* on an **epic**: the epic plus only child features whose frontmatter `cites:` includes `{epic_id}#{section_slug}`;
  (c) else, *section thread* on a **feature**, or any *doc-level* thread: the commented doc and all its children.
  A root is a section thread iff stored `section` **as-is** equals `section_slug(h)` for some current `##` or deeper heading on that doc; otherwise it is doc-level (H1, `general`, unmatched, historical free-text). Do not re-slugify stored section on read. Section is never empty.
  Tasks inherit blocking from their parent feature. `blocking_threads_for(work_id)` loads roots from the work **and its ancestors** (parent feature, parent epic). Slugs come from one shared `cascade.comments.section_slug` (feat_016, dec_006). `WorkMeta.cites` is feature-tier only. epic_002 children still record cites in spec body, not frontmatter (dec_019 known limitation).

## Core dependencies

- feat_005 comment sidecar + `CommentPosted` queue delivery
- feat_012 plan viewer (`GET /plan/{id}`, `/api/doc/{id}`)
- feat_004 / feat_005 epic & feature `reply_comment`, graph boot
- feat_014 workspace / worktree doc resolution for reads
- feat_016 comment fields, parent-as-reply, `section_slug()`, View plan `#plan-comments` (completed 2026-10-20). HTTP kickoff stayed out (dec_012, dec_021, dec_027). feat_016 D4/D5 merge note is void.

# Epic, feature, and task numbering

## Intent

Replace globally sequential work-item identifiers with stable hierarchical identifiers that reveal parentage:

- Epic: `epic_NNN`
- Feature: `feat_NNN_MMM`, where `NNN` is the parent epic number
- Task: `task_NNN_MMM_KKK`, where the first two segments identify the parent feature

Segments are zero-padded to three digits for readable lexical ordering. This epic changes identity and allocation only; titles, lifecycle states, and planning workflow remain unchanged.

### Success criteria

- Every newly created epic, feature, and task receives the canonical hierarchical form.
- Epic numbers remain globally unique; feature numbers are allocated within an epic; task numbers are allocated within a feature.
- Allocation is collision-safe and does not reuse an identifier merely because an item was moved, archived, or deleted.
- New features and tasks created beneath pre-existing epics still derive their hierarchy from the numeric segment of the existing parent ID.
- Every backlog epic and all of its descendant features and tasks are migrated immediately, including board-owned dependencies, citations, parent/child links, paths, and other stored references.
- Active and completed work keeps its existing identifier; those identifiers remain readable and operable during the compatibility period.
- Creation and migration failures do not leave a partially renamed work graph.
- High-signal integration coverage proves creation at all three tiers, sibling numbering in separate parents, compatibility with retained IDs, and backlog-graph migration.

## Macro-architecture

Use one canonical work-ID module for formatting, parsing, validation, and next-child allocation. Creation entry points must ask this module for an ID rather than reconstructing numbering rules.

Allocation reads the relevant namespace: all epics for a new epic, direct features for a new feature, and direct tasks for a new task. Within the existing board persistence boundary, each namespace also retains an authoritative high-water mark (or equivalent durable allocation history) so a hard-deleted identifier is never reused. Under the board process lock, allocation chooses one above both the persisted maximum and the high-water mark, then persists the new work item and advanced mark atomically; collision detection remains a defensive retry.

Treat backlog migration as a graph rewrite. Build and validate the complete old-to-new mapping first, then rewrite documents, paths, metadata, relationships, dependencies, citations, and board indexes as one recoverable operation. Emit a deterministic dry-run/report so operators can inspect mappings and diagnose conflicts.

Readers accept both retained legacy identifiers and the new hierarchical identifiers. Writers emit only hierarchical identifiers after rollout.

## Cross-module constraints

- Canonical prefixes remain `epic`, `feat`, and `task`; separators are underscores and each numeric segment is three digits.
- IDs are immutable after creation except for the explicit backlog migration in this epic.
- Numeric allocation is based on persisted identity plus durable allocation history, not list position or title; deleting the highest-numbered item must not lower the namespace high-water mark.
- Parentage encoded in a new ID must match the stored parent link; validation rejects disagreement.
- References must be rewritten by structured identity, never by unrestricted text replacement.
- User-authored prose mentioning an old ID is not rewritten unless it is a board-owned structured reference.
- Existing active/completed IDs remain valid inputs; no broad historical renumbering is in scope.
- The migration must be idempotent, detect target collisions before mutation, initialize or advance every affected namespace's durable high-water mark to at least the greatest assigned segment, and produce an audit mapping.
- Tests should concentrate on creation workflows and a representative graph migration; exhaustive unit coverage of trivial format helpers is unnecessary.

## Core dependencies

- The existing board process lock and Git-backed isolated-index commit boundary, extended narrowly for a prevalidated multi-path graph write with byte-level rollback.
- The authoritative indexes and serializers for work metadata and graph relationships.
- All creation interfaces that currently mint epic, feature, or task IDs.

No new external service or datastore is required.

## Architecture validation

### Recoverable graph-wide writes

The existing primitives are individually insufficient as-is: `write_doc` commits one document and does not restore it after commit failure; `save_doc` restores one path; and the worktree registry's temp-file/`os.replace` transaction applies only to that registry. The narrowest reusable boundary is the existing board `process_lock` plus `commit_paths` isolated-index commit.

The migration implementation must add one board-level graph-write operation that, while holding `process_lock`:

1. computes and validates the full mapping and every rendered destination before mutation;
2. rejects duplicate sources, occupied destinations, invalid parentage, and unresolved structured references;
3. snapshots bytes and existence for every affected board-owned path;
4. writes new files and removes old paths;
5. commits the entire affected path set once through `commit_paths`; and
6. restores the complete snapshot and invalidates board caches if any write or commit fails.

A deterministic manifest records the mapping and affected paths. Re-running after success is a no-op; re-running after a failed attempt starts from the restored pre-migration graph.

### ID persistence outside board documents

Cascade persists work IDs outside plan frontmatter and structured document references in local LangGraph checkpoint filenames/thread IDs, event queues, War Room chat and comment sidecars, the integration-worktree registry and paths, local Git branch names, and commit trailers. For this epic, assume no external integration currently persists Cascade work IDs.

Those local artifacts belong to active execution, while this epic migrates backlog graphs only. Migration therefore does not rename or rewrite runtime artifacts. Before mutation, it must prove the entire selected graph is backlog-only and reject it if any integration-worktree registration, matching local integration branch, checkpoint, or queue/runtime sidecar exists. Board-owned backlog comment/chat sidecars, if present, are included in the structured rewrite and atomic path set. The dry-run report lists every checked local artifact class and any blocker. External-system discovery, migration, and notification are out of scope under the explicit assumption that no external integration currently persists Cascade work IDs; that assumption must be revisited before such an integration is introduced.

## Feature breakdown

1. **feat_009 — Hierarchical ID allocation for new work**
   - Define the canonical parser/formatter/validator, scoped allocation rules, and durable per-namespace high-water marks within the existing board persistence boundary.
   - Integrate all epic, feature, and task creation paths.
   - Preserve read compatibility for retained identifiers.
   - Add creation-level integration coverage, including separate parent namespaces, collision handling, and non-reuse after deletion of the highest allocated item.

2. **feat_010 — Backlog epic ID migration** (depends on `feat_009`)
   - Discover backlog epic graphs and generate deterministic old-to-new mappings.
   - Validate collisions, reference coverage, backlog-only status, and absence of local runtime identity artifacts before changing state.
   - Rewrite board-owned documents, metadata, paths, indexes, cross-work references, applicable board sidecars, and affected durable allocation high-water marks in one locked Git commit with full byte-snapshot rollback.
   - Provide dry-run/audit output and representative end-to-end migration coverage, including injected commit failure and runtime-artifact refusal.
   - Leave active and completed work untouched.

## Explicit non-goals

- Renumbering active or completed epics and their existing descendants.
- Renaming local integration branches, worktrees, checkpoints, or queues.
- Changing lifecycle states, board ordering, titles, or human-readable slugs.
- Rewriting arbitrary user prose that merely contains an old identifier.
- Introducing configurable segment widths, alternate separators, or a general-purpose ID framework.
- Adding a new external coordination service solely for number allocation.

## Open questions

_(none)_

## Decision log

- 2026-10-21 · Human · Brief approved through merge request review.

- `dec_001` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Manager · **Identifier format and allocation**
  Chose Use epic_NNN, feat_NNN_MMM, and task_NNN_MMM_KKK with three-digit underscore-separated segments; allocate child segments monotonically within their direct parent..
  Rationale: The format makes parentage visible, preserves lexical ordering, matches existing canonical prefixes, and limits the change to identity semantics.
  Honors: The human request for hierarchical epic, feature, and task numbering..

- `dec_002` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Manager · **Migration scope**
  Chose Immediately migrate backlog epic graphs and board-owned structured references, while retaining active and completed identifiers as compatible inputs..
  Rationale: This meets the explicit backlog requirement without taking on a high-risk historical rewrite whose product value is low.
  Honors: The success criterion that backlog epics receive hierarchical numbering right away and the frugal-engineering constraint to avoid unnecessary scope..

- `dec_003` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Manager · **Feature sequencing**
  Chose Deliver canonical allocation and compatibility in feat_009 before the dependent backlog graph migration in feat_010..
  Rationale: Migration needs one settled parser, formatter, and allocation contract; separating it from steady-state creation makes rollout and verification recoverable.
  Honors: The smallest shippable sequence that keeps the system honest..

- `dec_004` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Architect · **Recoverable graph-wide migration**
  Chose Use one board-level graph-write operation under the existing process lock: prevalidate the full mapping, snapshot all affected bytes, mutate paths, commit the complete path set once through commit_paths, and restore the snapshot on any failure..
  Rationale: Existing write_doc and save_doc recovery is document-scoped, while the registry's atomic replacement is registry-specific. Extending the existing lock and isolated-index Git commit boundary is the narrowest mechanism that can make the whole board graph recoverable without adding a datastore or transaction framework.
  Honors: Collision safety, atomic migration, idempotence, and the frugal-engineering preference for the smallest reliable extension..

- `dec_005` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Architect · **Runtime and external ID artifacts**
  Chose Migrate only graphs proven backlog-only and free of runtime or published identity artifacts; reject graphs with worktree registrations, integration branches, checkpoints, queues, or remote review artifacts instead of renaming those systems. Rewrite board-owned backlog sidecars within the atomic migration..
  Rationale: Cascade persists IDs in local execution state and Git/forge identities, but those artifacts arise after dispatch and publication. A strict preflight preserves the approved backlog-only scope and avoids unsafe cross-system renames; retained active and completed IDs remain readable.
  Honors: The explicit compatibility boundary, no partial migration, and the requirement to define an external persistence contract before shipping..

- `dec_006` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Manager · **Architecture validation**
  Chose Assume no external integration currently persists Cascade work IDs; omit remote-system preflight, migration, and notification from this epic while retaining checks for local runtime identity artifacts..
  Rationale: This records the human-confirmed current-state boundary and avoids speculative integration work. Local checkpoints, queues, worktrees, and branches still exist and can make a backlog rename unsafe.
  Honors: In reply to: cmt_001; the human direction to assume no external integrations persist work IDs, plus the approved backlog-only and atomic-migration constraints..

- `dec_007` · 2026-10-22 · Epic Architect · **Allocation history**
  Chose Retain a durable high-water mark (or equivalent allocation history) for each epic, feature, and task namespace, and atomically advance it with creation under the existing board process lock..
  Rationale: Scanning only currently persisted siblings would reuse the highest identifier after hard deletion, contradicting the approved monotonic non-reuse requirement. A small persisted watermark closes that gap without introducing a new service or general transaction system.
  Honors: The epic success criterion that moved, archived, or deleted work IDs are never reused, and the frugal-engineering preference for the smallest reliable persistence extension..

- `dec_008` · 2026-10-22 · Epic Architect · **Migration allocation history**
  Chose During backlog graph migration, initialize or advance each affected epic, feature, and task namespace high-water mark to at least the greatest segment assigned by the migration, and include those updates in the same locked, snapshotted, single-commit graph write..
  Rationale: Migrated documents make the current maximum discoverable only while they remain present. If the highest migrated item is later hard-deleted and migration did not seed durable allocation history, a subsequent creation could reuse its identifier. Updating the existing feat_009 watermark state preserves monotonic non-reuse without adding a new persistence mechanism.
  Honors: The epic's non-reuse success criterion, the recoverable all-or-nothing migration boundary, and the frugal-engineering preference to extend existing allocation state..
## Amendment log

- 2026-10-22 · Architectural clarification for feat_010 · Required backlog migration to initialize or advance affected durable allocation high-water marks within the same recoverable graph write, preventing reuse of migrated IDs after later deletion.

- 2026-10-22 · Architectural clarification for feat_009 · Required durable per-namespace allocation history and atomic high-water-mark advancement so hard deletion cannot cause ID reuse; added one high-signal deletion/non-reuse integration criterion.

- 2026-10-21 · In reply to: cmt_001 · Adopted the current-state assumption that no external integration persists Cascade work IDs. Removed remote-system preflight and migration requirements while retaining local runtime-artifact refusal and the recoverable graph-write boundary.

# Lifecycle management

## Intent

Make approval, dependency dispatch, completion rollup, and merge-request review predictable across the feature and epic lifecycle.

A feature may be approved independently. Epic approval approves every child feature that exists at that time, but implementation dispatch occurs only after the feature is approved, all declared feature dependencies are complete, and the existing merge gate permits another feature to start.

A feature completes only after its tasks are complete and its merge request has merged. An epic completes automatically when all persisted child features are complete. A proposed follow-up blocks that rollup only after it has been accepted and minted as a child feature.

Reviewers can see all open merge requests in a dedicated War Room view and navigate directly to each review.

### Success criteria

- Per-feature and epic-wide approval are durable and dispatch respects approval and `depends_on` completion.
- Feature completion requires completed tasks plus a merged MR.
- Epic completion rolls up automatically from all persisted child features.
- An accepted, persisted follow-up keeps the epic active; an unaccepted suggestion does not.
- War Room provides an Open MRs view backed by the existing durable review registry.
- Lifecycle reconciliation is idempotent after restart.
- One economical sandbox/browser scenario demonstrates the critical lifecycle and review behavior.

## Macro-architecture

Lifecycle decisions remain in existing authoritative services and durable registries:

1. The central dispatch path evaluates durable feature approval, completed dependencies, and the existing one-feature-awaiting-merge constraint.
2. A lifecycle reconciler derives feature completion from task completion plus MR merge state, then derives epic completion from child-feature state; reconciliation is restart-safe and idempotent.
3. A read-only reviews API queries the existing durable review registry.
4. War Room renders Open MRs from that API with direct review links.
5. A disposable system fixture drives public lifecycle entry points to demonstrate the full flow.

No parallel approval, lifecycle, or review store is introduced.

## Cross-module constraints

- Approval is durable state separate from board lifecycle status.
- All implementation entry points pass through one dispatch eligibility check.
- Dependency readiness means every feature in `depends_on` is completed.
- Epic approval applies to children present at approval time; later children require explicit approval.
- Feature completion cannot precede MR merge.
- Epic completion is derived, never manually asserted by this flow.
- Only a follow-up persisted as a child feature participates in completion rollup.
- Review UI and API read from the existing review registry and do not duplicate review state.
- Preserve the current single-feature-awaiting-merge gate.
- Child metadata is authoritative for dispatch; the current titles and dependency edges are aligned with the sequence below.
- Prefer focused integration coverage plus one system/browser scenario; do not create a new test framework if an existing harness suffices.

## Core dependencies

- Existing approval persistence and commands.
- Central dispatch/orchestration and the `depends_on` graph.
- Task completion state and durable merge-request/review registry.
- Lifecycle reconciliation and restart recovery.
- War Room API/frontend routing and the existing browser/system test harness.

## Feature breakdown

1. **feat_001 — Approval and dependency dispatch**
   - Persist per-feature approval and epic-wide approval of current children.
   - Gate central dispatch on approval, completed dependencies, and the existing merge constraint.
2. **feat_002 — Completion rollup and recovery** (depends on feat_001)
   - Complete features after tasks finish and their MR merges.
   - Roll completion up across persisted children and recover idempotently.
3. **feat_003 — Open review registry API** (depends on feat_001 and feat_002)
   - Expose an authoritative read-only open-review model with feature/epic context and direct URLs.
4. **feat_004 — Lifecycle sandbox demonstration** (depends on feat_001 and feat_002)
   - Prove approval, dependency gating, merge ordering, recovery, and rollup through one disposable system scenario.
5. **feat_005 — Open merge requests War Room view** (depends on feat_003 and feat_004)
   - Render Open MRs and usable states, with direct review links.
   - Extend the scenario only enough to prove appearance and disappearance after merge.

## Open questions

- No unresolved epic-level planning questions. Feature planning should reuse existing lifecycle, review, and test abstractions.

## Decision log

- 2026-10-21 · Human · Brief approved through merge request review.

- `dec_001` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Team · **Lifecycle approval and dispatch**
  Chose to keep approval as durable state separate from board lifecycle status and enforce approval plus dependency readiness in the central dispatch path.
  Rationale: Approval and status answer different questions; a single dispatch guard prevents bypasses.
  Honors: Per-feature approval, epic-wide approval of current children, dependency-safe dispatch, and restart recovery.

- `dec_002` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Team · **Completion rollup**
  Chose to derive feature completion from completed tasks plus a merged MR, and epic completion from all persisted child-feature states.
  Rationale: Derived state avoids premature or divergent completion and supports idempotent recovery.
  Honors: Automatic feature and epic transitions based on content completion.

- `dec_003` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Team · **Follow-up semantics**
  Chose to make a follow-up completion-blocking only after acceptance and minting as a child feature.
  Rationale: Persisted children provide an auditable boundary without a second backlog state.
  Honors: Keeping an epic active for accepted follow-up work.

- `dec_004` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Team · **Review dashboard**
  Chose to build the Open MRs API and War Room view from the existing durable review registry.
  Rationale: One authoritative registry minimizes synchronization failure.
  Honors: Easy access to open merge requests.

- `dec_005` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Team · **Verification strategy**
  Chose focused lifecycle integration tests and one browser/system flow over broad redundant unit coverage.
  Rationale: This covers high-value boundaries and recovery with lower maintenance cost.
  Honors: Pragmatic validation and a Playwright-style demonstration.

- `dec_006` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Team · **Feature sequencing after concurrent mint**
  Chose Retain the five minted children but remove overlap: feat_003 owns the read-only review API, feat_004 owns the lifecycle sandbox scenario, and feat_005 owns the War Room UI; feat_005 waits for both API and sandbox..
  Rationale: Concurrent planning minted two additional children after the original three-feature breakdown. Giving each a narrow, independently verifiable boundary avoids duplicate implementation and preserves an ordered smallest-coherent delivery without inventing unrelated scope.
  Honors: The requested sandbox demonstration, Open MRs dashboard, dependency-safe sequencing, and frugal high-signal testing..

- `dec_007` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Architect · **Feature metadata as dispatch contract**
  Chose Treat child feature metadata as authoritative for dispatch and block approval of feat_004 and feat_005 until their titles and dependency edges match the epic sequence..
  Rationale: Feature-body prose cannot enforce orchestration order. The current metadata omits feat_002 from feat_004 and feat_003 from feat_005, which could bypass required lifecycle/API prerequisites.
  Honors: Dependency-safe dispatch, artifact-driven alignment, and the smallest coherent delivery sequence..

- `dec_008` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Manager · **Metadata reconciliation**
  Chose Treat the corrected child titles and dependency edges as authoritative and clear the pre-approval dispatch blocker..
  Rationale: Board metadata now matches the epic sequence: feat_004 depends on feat_001 and feat_002, while feat_005 depends on feat_003 and feat_004; the stale titles for feat_003 through feat_005 are also aligned.
  Honors: Dependency-safe dispatch, artifact-driven alignment, and the smallest coherent five-feature plan..

- `dec_009` · 2026-10-21 · Epic Architect · **Architecture readiness after metadata reconciliation**
  Chose Accept the reconciled five-feature architecture and dependency graph as ready for sequenced delivery..
  Rationale: Authoritative child metadata now matches the epic contract: feat_002 follows feat_001; feat_003 and feat_004 follow the lifecycle foundation; feat_005 follows both the review API and lifecycle demonstration. The slices remain non-overlapping and use focused integration coverage plus one system flow.
  Honors: Dependency-safe dispatch, artifact-driven alignment, durable lifecycle state, one authoritative review registry, and frugal high-signal verification..

# Use provider API to offer list of models in brief

## Intent

Brief creation must not accept provider/model combinations that downstream agents cannot use. Replace free-text model entry with choices discovered from installed, authenticated provider APIs, and capture defaults for every role layer created from the brief.

The initial delivery validates this at brief-creation time without introducing a background synchronization service.

### Success criteria

- The provider selector contains only providers that are installed/configured and successfully report availability.
- Offered models come from the selected provider's actual API response; the UI does not own a static model list.
- Brief creation uses selectors, not arbitrary model text, for all configured epic, feature, and task roles.
- For providers and models that support configurable reasoning, brief creation offers supported reasoning levels for each role, including the provider default; unsupported combinations use their default without a selector.
- The selected provider and per-role model defaults are persisted and used by downstream work creation.
- Selected per-role reasoning levels are persisted and used by downstream work creation; leaving a level at default preserves provider behavior.
- One unavailable or failing provider does not prevent healthy providers from being offered.
- When no provider is usable, submission is disabled with a clear, recoverable state.
- A representative end-to-end test covers discovery, selection, persistence, and reload/use of saved defaults.

## Macro-architecture

1. Each provider integration exposes capability discovery returning its canonical provider identifier, current models, and supported reasoning levels or default behavior for each model when available.
2. A provider inventory service queries only installed/configured integrations, isolates adapter failures, normalizes results, and applies a small bounded freshness cache around successful responses.
3. The existing application boundary exposes that inventory to brief creation, including loading, empty-availability, and refresh-failure states.
4. The brief UI selects one available provider and renders model selectors for every epic, feature, and task role represented by the brief schema. For models with configurable reasoning, it also renders a per-role reasoning selector with a default choice. Changing provider or model clears or revalidates incompatible selections.
5. The existing brief write path validates selections against the current inventory, persists provider plus per-role model and reasoning defaults, and supplies those defaults when downstream feature and task work is minted.

Provider-specific API and authentication behavior stays inside existing integrations; the UI consumes one normalized contract.

## Cross-module constraints

- Provider APIs are authoritative for selectable models. Static UI model catalogs are out of scope.
- Credentials and raw provider errors must not cross the application boundary or appear in client-visible responses/logs.
- Discovery is fault-isolated: one timeout, missing login, or absent installation makes only that provider unavailable.
- Cache freshness must be explicit and bounded. Refresh on expiry or user request is sufficient; a scheduler or durable background job is not required.
- The server revalidates submitted provider/model identifiers; client selectors are not a trust boundary.
- The server also validates non-default reasoning levels against the selected provider/model capability; unsupported combinations cannot accept an override.
- Existing saved briefs with unavailable historical values remain readable; this epic governs new or edited selections and does not require migration.
- Reuse the existing brief schema and role naming. Expand it only where full-stack defaults cannot already be represented.
- Concentrate tests on the provider inventory boundary and one end-to-end brief flow; redundant per-component coverage is not required.

## Core dependencies

- Existing provider integration registry/configuration and authentication state.
- Provider APIs that enumerate usable models.
- Existing brief creation/read persistence boundary.
- Existing propagation path from epic defaults to feature/task work.

No new external service, durable cache, or scheduler is a prerequisite.

## Feature breakdown

1. **feat_006_001 — Discover available providers and models**
   - Add normalized discovery across installed/configured provider integrations.
- Expose supported reasoning levels and default behavior where a provider/model offers configurable reasoning.
   - Filter unavailable providers, isolate partial failures, and apply bounded caching/refresh.
   - Expose a safe UI-facing inventory contract.
   - Prove API-derived results, filtering, partial failure, and refresh behavior.

2. **feat_006_002 — Select provider and full-stack model defaults in brief**  
   Depends on: feat_006_001
   - Replace free-text model fields with inventory-backed selectors.
   - Cover all epic, feature, and task roles represented by the brief schema, including per-role reasoning selectors when supported and a default choice.
   - Validate and persist model and reasoning selections, then propagate them through downstream work creation.
   - Cover loading/empty/error states and one representative end-to-end flow.

## Non-goals

- A continuously running or durable provider synchronization subsystem.
- Model pricing, benchmarking, recommendation, ranking, or automatic “best model” selection.
- Installing providers or signing users into providers from the brief screen.
- Migrating or rewriting historical briefs.
- Supporting arbitrary model identifiers that the provider API did not return.

## Open questions

- During feature planning, map the existing brief-schema role keys to the epic/feature/task selectors; preserve current role names.
- Confirm each provider's model-list API and authentication probe. A provider without safe enumeration remains unavailable rather than falling back to a hard-coded list.
- Choose the shortest cache TTL that avoids noisy calls while keeping availability credible; this is an implementation parameter, not a product promise.

## Decision log

- 2026-10-21 · Human · Brief approved through merge request review.
- 2026-10-24 · Epic Manager · Deliver provider discovery as a shared, fault-isolated backend inventory before changing the brief UI.
- 2026-10-24 · Epic Manager · Use bounded on-demand caching; exclude periodic background synchronization from the initial scope.
- 2026-10-24 · Epic Manager · Use one selected provider with per-role model defaults across epic, feature, and task layers; reject arbitrary new model text.
- 2026-10-24 · Epic Manager · Preserve historical briefs without migration; validate new or edited selections against current discovery.
- 2026-10-24 · Human · Include supported reasoning-level overrides in brief selectors; retain provider defaults when no override is chosen.

- `dec_001` · 2026-10-24 · Epic Manager · **Architecture sequencing**
  Chose Establish a shared, fault-isolated provider/model inventory before replacing brief inputs..
  Rationale: Provider availability and model validation need one authoritative boundary; otherwise the UI would duplicate provider-specific behavior and cannot isolate failures.
  Honors: Success criteria requiring only available providers and models obtained from provider APIs..

- `dec_002` · 2026-10-24 · Epic Manager · **Refresh policy**
  Chose Use bounded on-demand caching with expiry or explicit refresh; do not build periodic background synchronization in the initial epic..
  Rationale: It avoids repeated API calls while keeping the first delivery small; durable scheduling adds operational cost without being required to validate briefs.
  Honors: The brief's suggestion that asynchronous refresh is optional, plus the frugal smallest-shippable-slice constraint..

- `dec_003` · 2026-10-24 · Epic Manager · **Configuration contract**
  Chose Select one provider and persist model defaults for every existing epic, feature, and task role; reject arbitrary model text for new or edited selections..
  Rationale: A shared provider matches the current brief contract while per-role models satisfy full-stack configuration and prevent invalid downstream values.
  Honors: Success criteria requiring model choice for the full agent stack..

- `dec_004` · 2026-10-24 · Epic Manager · **Compatibility**
  Chose Keep historical briefs readable without migration, while validating new or edited selections against current discovery..
  Rationale: Provider catalogs change; forcing migration is costly and could make prior artifacts unreadable, while validation still protects newly created downstream work.
  Honors: Core reliability without expanding scope into historical data migration..
